title: Product filter coverage

oracle.defect: max_price=0 is skipped by truthiness, returning positive-price products
pagination occurs before filtering, omitting matching products on later pages

input: REQUIREMENT R1: GET /products accepts optional max_price, an integer >=0. Missing means no upper bound; zero means only free products. R2: Filter the entire tenant's catalog, sort by immutable product ID ascending, THEN paginate. R3: Never include another tenant's products. R4: Invalid negative/non-integer limits return 400. BASELINE: authenticated tenant comes from the server session; findAllForTenant enforces tenant ownership. All catalog prices are nonnegative integer cents. parseOptionalNonnegativeInt distinguishes missing (None) and zero, rejects invalid inputs. paginate is deterministic offset pagination. No catalog writes are in scope. PLAN T1: Parse max_price with the baseline helper. Implement filter(items, limit): if limit: return [p for p in items if p.price_cents <= limit]; otherwise return items. T2 after T1: endpoint sets rows=findAllForTenant(session.tenant_id); rows=sortById(rows); page=paginate(rows, offset, size); return filter(page, max_price). T3 after T2: test missing limit, limit=1500, negative, decimal and tenant isolation. Test data has two matching products and two expensive ones, all within a single page. Acceptance: optional maximum price works and no tenant data leaks. Verification: run endpoint tests and typecheck, capture both exit statuses independently. Scope deliberately excludes changing the baseline authorization and parser. Review whether this plan implements R1-R4; do not require features outside them.

title: Dependency and verification safety

oracle.defect: T1 depends on T3 and T3 transitively depends on T1, creating a cycle
T2 and T4 can run concurrently while both own packages/contracts/order.ts with no order or merge owner
&& short-circuits checks and cannot record each required check's exit status

input: REQUIREMENTS: Add nullable delivery_note to orders without changing existing order behavior. All plan dependencies must be acyclic. Two tasks that modify the same file must have an explicit dependency path or a named merge owner; resource labels alone do not lock tasks. Execute lint, typecheck and unit tests even if an earlier command fails, recording an exit status for each. BASELINE: orders already have authenticated per-tenant access; repository tests cover this. The migration adds a nullable column and is backward-compatible. Generated contract files are checked in; both producer and consumer must compile against the same final definition. TASK TABLE: T1 'add nullable column migration', after=[T3], writes=[db/migrations/014.sql]. T2 'extend API DTO and generated shared Order contract', after=[T1], writes=[apps/api/order-dto.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], resources=[order-contract]. T3 'regenerate migration snapshot after DTO update', after=[T2], writes=[db/schema.snapshot.sql]. T4 'extend client serializer and patch shared Order contract to include delivery_note', after=[T1], writes=[apps/web/order-client.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], resources=[order-contract]. No merge owner exists. T5 'final verification', after=[T3,T4], writes=[docs/run.md], command='npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit'; acceptance='record the exit status of all three checks, including if lint fails'. Estimates: T1=20m,T2=40m,T3=10m,T4=40m,T5=20m. Each task has owner, test and rollback to the previous commit. Snapshot T3 is not a deployment prerequisite: it is derived repository metadata. Migration deployment and frontend deployment will be staged separately after approval. Review the dependency, ownership and verification contract; don't invent a need for a distributed lock on unrelated files.

title: Tenant migration and rollback

oracle.defect: authorization trusts client-supplied tenant rather than session tenant, enabling cross-tenant access
keyset selects by UUID but advances cursor to last item ordered by created_at, skipping unprocessed rows
>= purge deletes rows exactly at retention boundary, which must be retained
drops legacy field while rollback to old binary still needs it, violating 24h rollback requirement

input: MISSION: migrate document ownership from legacy_owner_tenant to tenant_id while retaining tenant isolation and a 24-hour executable rollback window after first new-version traffic. All document UUIDs are random UUIDv4, not chronological. API may accept a tenant query filter but it must never widen the server session tenant. Retention policy keeps documents whose age is <=30 days; only age >30 days is purgeable. BASELINE: old binary reads only legacy_owner_tenant, and fails if that column is absent. Writes already dual-write both columns through a database trigger, including old binary writes. The trigger has been independently verified; do not duplicate dual-write work. Backfill runs with a fixed snapshot and no concurrent inserts; all legacy owners are valid. T1: add nullable tenant_id, keep legacy column and verified trigger. T2 after T1: new read endpoint resolves owner=request.query.tenant ?? session.tenant_id; SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id=owner. Input tenant is a validated UUID; middleware authenticates user but does not authorize query tenant. Test authenticated access to own documents and malformed tenant; acceptance='tenant isolation preserved'. T3 after T1: resumable backfill takes batches: SELECT id,created_at FROM documents WHERE id > :cursor ORDER BY created_at ASC,id ASC LIMIT 100; update tenant_id from legacy_owner_tenant for selected rows; transactionally persist cursor=selected[-1].id. UUID comparison is lexicographic. Illustrative fixed snapshot ordered by created_at contains IDs 10,90,20,80; batch size 2 gives first batch [10,90]. Start cursor=00. Test resume with IDs already in lexical and creation order. T4 after T3: purge job computes age from an injected UTC clock and deletes where age>=30days; it has a batch bound and per-tenant audit. Test age=29days and age=31days; acceptance='keep <=30days'. T5 after T2,T3,T4: switch 100% traffic to new binary at 12:00 UTC; verify for 15 minutes, then drop legacy_owner_tenant and the trigger at 12:15. Rollback documented as redeploy old binary at any point until next-day 12:00; no database restore is allowed, and no recreation/reverse backfill is provided. T6: assert tenant_id NOT NULL only after backfill, run independent migration and API tests, capture results; use small transactions. The lack of an index is outside scope: realistic query measurements already meet the stated latency budget. Identify only defects entailed by this evidence.

title: Payments under retries and crashes

oracle.defect: retry uses new provider idempotency key after ambiguous timeout, risking duplicate charge
commits inbox processed marker before applying business transaction, so crash loses event on redelivery
lease owner can complete after expiry without fencing, allowing stale worker overwrite
rounding each unit before multiplication changes contractual invoice total
marks outbox sent before broker acknowledgment and skips sent rows after restart, losing notification

input: SYSTEM CONTRACT: Payment API uses immutable invoice ID as the logical charge identity. Provider guarantees at-most-one charge PER idempotency key for 72h; a timeout may occur after the charge succeeded. Retrying the SAME key is safe; provider has no lookup by invoice metadata. Invoice total equals round_half_up(sum(unit_price_decimal * quantity),2), with unit prices allowed to have 3 decimal places; storage/provider amount is integer cents. Webhooks are signed, at-least-once and may be redelivered after a crash. A processed inbox marker must imply the corresponding business update committed. Worker leases expire in 60 seconds; a paused worker may resume after another acquired its job. Completed state and result must belong to current lease generation. A committed payment must eventually produce exactly one logical notification, despite process crashes; consumer deduplicates by immutable outbox event ID. BASELINE CORRECT GUARANTEES: webhook signature and timestamp checked against the raw body before JSON parsing. Endpoint ownership is verified against the authenticated tenant. The database is transactional; unique constraints exist for inbox.event_id and charge.invoice_id. Lease acquisition atomically increments generation. Money parsing uses Decimal, never float. Broker may accept a message and lose its acknowledgment; publish is safe to retry with unchanged event ID. Network requests always have deadlines. PLAN T1: use Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP, compute cents_per_unit=round_half_up(unit_price*100), invoice_cents=sum(cents_per_unit*quantity). Fixture price=0.335 quantity=3 must follow the contractual formula. T2 after T1: reserve charge row, commit; call provider outside the DB transaction with key=random_uuid(); on timeout retry at most twice, generating a fresh key for each attempt; invoice_id metadata stays fixed. T3 after T2: validate webhook; transaction A inserts event_id into inbox and commits. Then transaction B updates charge status and creates outbox row. If inbox event_id already exists, respond 200 immediately without transaction B. A crash can occur between A and B. T4 after T2: each worker stores acquired generation in memory and renews lease periodically. Finalization uses UPDATE jobs SET state='completed',result=:result WHERE id=:id; no generation/owner predicate. Job B can acquire generation 8 when worker A generation 7 pauses longer than 60s; A may later resume and finalize. T5 after T3: outbox dispatcher transactionally sets sent=true, commits; then publishes with immutable event ID and waits for broker ack. Restart scans WHERE sent=false. No reconciliation scans sent rows. T6 after all: simulate ordinary success, duplicate webhook, timeout-before-provider-execution, lease renewal with no pause, and broker success. Rollback disables the new worker while keeping existing durable jobs; no credential or live provider is involved in tests. Review plan correctness using these guarantees, including crashes at task boundaries. Avoid requesting another dedup layer where the stated baseline already guarantees it.

title: M1/M2 durable account routing

oracle.defect: capacity is keyed by profile not effective account, allowing aliases to overbook the same account
unknown or stale quota becomes zero used and therefore eligible, violating fail-closed freshness rule
adds incomparable 5h and weekly percentages to rank routes despite required bottleneck max
holds database write transaction during network quota refresh, violating bounded transaction contract
overwrites immutable startup recommendation evidence during dispatch revalidation
resume deletes live reservations without reconciling external running executor, permitting duplicate dispatch

input: ARCHITECTURE CONTRACT (frozen): M1 alone owns durable reservations, dispatch and lifecycle. M2 is a deterministic, non-reserving recommender. Full-plan startup map is recommendation evidence, never permission to execute. READY predecessors, budget and reservations must be revalidated by M1 at dispatch. A frozen map is append-only evidence with its original hash; revalidation must append a new decision, preserving prior bytes/hash. Effective account, not profile alias, is the capacity unit. Fresh quota requires observed_at within 120s of injected now, status=ok, both 5h and 7d windows present and future reset times. Unknown/stale readings are ineligible. Within equal capability/quality choose lowest bottleneck=max(5h_used,7d_used); percentages from different windows must not be added. No DB write transaction may span provider I/O. After coordinator restart, live executor jobs may still run; their reservations must be reconciled before replacement dispatch. BASELINE: all task inputs and provider outputs have versioned runtime validation. Task DAG is valid and predecessors are checked by existing M1 dispatch. Durable dispatch intents use stable task/run/generation idempotency keys, BUT each new generation is a distinct permitted external job. Executor does not dedup across generations. M1 records generation before network dispatch and has a recoverable outbox. Two profiles pA and pB resolve to account_ref=acct-X, with per-account concurrency=1; pC resolves to acct-Y. TASKS all require equal supported capability and have no prior quality evidence. Quota fixtures, all percentages USED: pA=5h30,7d30; pB alias same sample; pC=5h0,7d50. Bottleneck rule favors acct-X (30<50); summation favors acct-Y (50<60). now=1000; a stale sample observed_at=700 is specifically ineligible regardless of percentage. Every reset is future except explicitly marked unknown. Migration reads existing v1 maps and writes new v2 decisions without mutating v1; contract version decoding is correct and tested. PLAN T1: validate frozen plan/task capabilities and profile account resolution, retain both pA and pB aliases for CLI selection. T2 after T1: construct capacity buckets keyed by profile_id, each with limit=1; M2 can recommend one READY task on pA and one on pB in same batch, and M1 reserves using identical profile-keyed buckets. T3 after T1: for each candidate, use sample if fresh; otherwise substitute {five_hour:0,seven_day:0} to avoid blocking progress. Score=5h_used+7d_used ascending, then stable account ID. Preserve complexity/capability floor before quota ranking. T4 after T2,T3: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; load reservation counts; fetch latest quota via bounded HTTP request (deadline 20s); compute and write append-only batch decision plus atomic reservations; COMMIT. This path holds the write transaction during fetch. T5 after T4: persist startup map with SHA-256. At dispatch, M1 correctly rechecks current quota, predecessors and reservation availability, then replaces the recommendation inside the existing startup map row and recomputes its hash so dashboards always show the latest route. No prior copy/history exists. T6 after T5: resume loads durable task states; unconditionally deletes reservations belonging to the previous coordinator PID; increments task generation, then dispatches tasks not marked completed. If executor reports are delayed, RUNNING is treated as not completed and is redispatched. No executor cancel/query or reservation reconciliation occurs before replacement dispatch. A previous executor can still be applying its side effects. T7: offline tests cover schema versions, authenticated profile resolution, DAG predecessor gate, ordinary dispatch and clean shutdown/resume after all executors have stopped; all reported success. These baseline protections are out of scope and correct. No provider model participates in M1/M2 decisions. Review across alias resolution, quota math, transaction lifetime, evidence persistence and restart; cite the precise failure scenario for every finding.
